title: Renewal Slate: Two-Track Deck + Playbook for Standard and Enterprise
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, reusable deck + playbook template intended for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) that double as renewal conversations. The design is two-track: a Growth track (Health -> Expansion asks) for healthy accounts, and a Risk track (Health -> Root-cause -> Remediation -> Renewal decision) for at-risk accounts. Use the Standard variant for < $50k ARR accounts and the Enterprise variant for strategic customers requiring cross-functional stakeholders, procurement readiness, and legal considerations.

High-level instructions (notes to presenter):
- Target length: 20 slides for Standard (~30–40 minutes) ; 30–40 slides for Enterprise (~60 minutes).
- Audience: primary executive sponsor, technical lead, procurement/legal as needed (enterprise).
- Prep checklist (2 days before): export product telemetry for last 90 days, refresh utilization and cost-per-feature metrics, gather 3 customer success stories, confirm stakeholders + meeting objectives.

Slide-by-slide outline (two-track, single template that can be toggled):
1) Cover + Objectives (1 slide)
   - Title, customer name, quarter, CS owner
   - Meeting goals: (pick 2–3) health review, renewal discussion, expansion opportunities
   - Speaker note: call out if this is primarily a renewal conversation up front

2) Executive snapshot (1 slide)
   - Top-line adoption metrics, NPS trend, support SLA attainment, renewal date & current ARR
   - Visual: 3 KPI tiles + 1 timeline (renewal date)

3) Two-track signpost (1 slide)
   - Visual switch: if HealthScore > threshold -> Growth track, else Risk track.
   - Quick guidance: which slides to skip/show for each track

Growth track (only show for healthy accounts)
4) Adoption deep-dive (2 slides)
   - Active users, key workloads, top 3 features by usage, latency and error trends
   - Speaker note: highlight wins tied to business outcomes

5) Value stories & wins (2 slides)
   - Short customer quotes, metrics improved (e.g. 2x throughput, 30% cost reduction)

6) Expansion opportunities (2 slides)
   - Product-led: feature flags, new modules; Commercial: seats, dedicated capacity
   - Ask ladder: Small pilot -> scoped expansion -> enterprise contract (example price bands)

7) Commercial recommendation (1 slide)
   - Proposed renewal term, list price vs. recommended discount, timeline for signature
   - Speaker play: anchor on outcomes first, price second

8) Implementation & success plan for expansion (2 slides)
   - Timeline, owner RACI, success criteria & KPIs

Risk track (only show for at-risk accounts)
4R) Health diagnose (2 slides)
   - Healthscore drivers, incidents, feature gaps, onboarding gaps. Include sample SQLs for metrics (see notes)

5R) Root causes & hypotheses (1 slide)
   - E.g., "low API throughput due to suboptimal batching config"

6R) Remediation plan (2 slides)
   - Short term actions (1–4 weeks), medium term (1–3 months), owners, dependencies

7R) Renewal options & escalation (1 slide)
   - Standard renew, pilot extension, survival pack (discount + success SLA), or churn path

Common appendices (show as needed)
- Appendix A: Detailed usage dashboards and SQL snippets (2 pages)
  - sample SQL: SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, count(distinct user_id) FROM requests WHERE org_id = {{org}} AND ts > now() - interval '90 days' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;
- Appendix B: Cost breakdown per feature (1 page)
- Appendix C: Contract summary + PO and procurement checklist (enterprise)
- Appendix D: Support case timeline & root cause artifacts

Renewal tracker sheet (instructions & columns to include):
- Suggested columns: customer_name, org_id, ARR_current, renewal_date, renewal_owner, health_score, top_risks (short text), recommended_next_action, commercial_recommendation, legal_ready (Y/N), procurement_contact, forecast_probability, last_contact_date.
- Weekly cadence: update tracker each Friday with a short note in the comments column describing any change in negotiations.

Stakeholder RACI (short template):
- Executive Sponsor: Account Exec (A), CS Lead (C), Procurement (I), Engineering (I)
- Technical Decision Maker: CS Lead (C), Solutions Eng (R), Eng Owner (I)
- Billing/PO sign-off: Sales Ops (R), Customer Procurement (A)

Risk scoring rubric (quick):
- HealthScore 0–100: >75 = Green, 50–75 = Yellow, <50 = Red
- Commercial risk modifiers: Net new competitor RFP (+20 risk), business restructuring (+30), support SLA breach last 30 days (+25)
- Convert to forecast probability: 80/60/30 for Green/Yellow/Red (adjust with commercial modifiers)

Speaker scripts & email templates (snippets):
- Renewal intro email (2 weeks prior): short pitch linking outcomes -> renewal ask -> proposed meeting times.
- Follow-up with procurement: include PO template, contact for order processing, and SOX/PCI checklist if relevant.

Negotiation playbook (enterprise-specific):
- Concessions ladder: limited pilot extension (1 month) -> add success SLA instead of price cut -> apply one-time credit -> multi-year price lock (final concession).
- Legal: use standard SOW addendum with explicit data handling clauses; escalate to LegalOps if customer requests custom clauses.

Operational callouts and warnings (notes to self):
- Avoid opening the meeting with price. Lead with outcomes.
- Have 1–2 success stories that match the sponsor's industry.
- If engineering is required, pre-book 30 minutes afterward for tech deep-dive; show appendix.

Design and visual guidance (quick):
- Use customer brand colors sparingly; Redwood colors for callouts.
- KPI tiles: big number, % delta vs prior quarter, one-line context.
- Use simple timelines and RACI tables in appendix.

Post-meeting actions (immediately after the call):
- Send meeting notes and proposed contract term within 24 hours.
- Create JIRA/Linear task for any remediation items and tag product/eng owners.
- Update renewal tracker with selected option and new forecast probability.

Open questions and TODOs (internal):
- Add specific enterprise procurement timeline examples per region (NA vs EU).
- Collect canonical legal templates from LegalOps for inclusion.
- Draft a short SLAs + SLO appendix that can be toggled per account.

Quick reference: canned slide names to copy into templates
- "Executive Snapshot", "Health Signpost", "Adoption & Usage", "Value Stories", "Expansion Roadmap", "Recommended Terms", "Remediation Plan", "Procurement Checklist"

Last notes: this doc is intentionally a working template — please add concrete examples and recent customer quotes before using live. Tag me (Maya Chen) in Slack #cs-renewals for review.
